Case for buying Jane now, weighed honestly:

That's real two-sided activity, not a single operator's bag. The curve is classed ORGANIC with a top-3 holder share of only 15%, and the first two minutes after graduation show 251 buyers ex-agent with top-5 buyer share at 18%.

The case has real holes, though. The 30-minute high has already been given back by 65%, and the last 15 minutes show sell SOL (711) nearly matching buy SOL (760), a sell-to-buy ratio near 0.9 post-graduation. Bundle share on the curve is 45%, a sign of coordinated early buying, and a launch bot was present. The metadata host is an unfamiliar domain. The pool is thin at 122 SOL, so exit costs will be high.

Verdict: the demand evidence is real but it's fading, and the drawdown plus bundled early buying point to a coin that has already peaked. I see no case strong enough to clear the base rate for a 30-60 minute hold. Skip.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss path is a rug or insider distribution after the 64% drawdown from the 30-minute high. The curve bundle share is 44.5%, and the completer holds 34.6% of curve activity, so a bundled cluster may be positioned to exit. In the last 15 minutes, sellers (838) nearly matched buyers (1,038), sell SOL (710.9) was 93% of buy SOL (760.4), and net flow was only +49.5 SOL, so exits are absorbing the bids. The pool is thin at 122 SOL, so a $20 ticket plus round-trip fees of 1.4-5.1% needs a move that this volatile coin may not give. The metadata host and the name "I Am Jane Doe" are unverified, so I'd treat that as a signal of low-effort launch. Recommendation: skip.
